definition: Returning the most frequent answer among sampled trajectories, counting every trajectory equally. The sources treat it as the aggregation floor and report it is hard to beat outright but easy to improve on when combined rather than replaced — two reward-model variants that individually lose to it both surpass it once their scores weight the vote. The archive now holds two accounts of why it fails when it fails. Mechanistically, incorrect trajectories converge to their wrong answer earlier than correct ones converge to the right one, so counting votes rewards the failure mode. Formally, its failure probability does not decay to zero at all: a wrong answer holding 46% against a right answer's 45% converges to the wrong one however many samples are drawn, which is the precise reason self-consistency saturates and then degrades, and the reason the tournament aggregations that do have vanishing failure probability are built on pairwise comparison instead. A third entry attacks its cost rather than its accuracy, stopping the sampling by a Bayesian posterior over which answer is the mode and proving that tracking the top two counts is asymptotically enough.

evidence.note: Shows that a perturbation-based selection rule's apparent 31.8-point gain over majority voting in vision-language test-time scaling is a decoding-format effect, by adding a control that spends the same short-answer budget on the unperturbed image and finds it matches or beats the perturbation rule everywhere.
evidence.title: It's the Decoding Format, Not the Perturbation: Auditing Consistency-Based Selection for Vision-Language Test-Time Scaling

evidence.note: Diagnoses label-free RLVR's collapse as a shortcut in which the same answer-level consensus signal both estimates the reward and receives the gradient, and fixes it by masking the answer span from updates entirely — so a reward can only be raised by improving the reasoning that produces the answer.
evidence.title: Don't Peek at the Answer: Outcome-Masked Group Relative Policy Optimization for Label-Free RLVR

evidence.note: Spends test-time compute on iteratively refining each sampled rollout rather than on drawing more of them, then majority-votes the refined answers, with no verifier.
evidence.title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Verifies correctness without training by comparing a reasoning trace's start-to-end hidden-state delta against two class centroids built from labelled experience.
evidence.title: Your Reasoning Model is Secretly a Reward Model - Optimization-Free Verification from Experience

evidence.note: Stops self-consistency sampling by Bayesian posterior over which answer is the mode, and proves that tracking only the top two answer counts plus an aggregate is enough for asymptotic optimality.
evidence.title: Optimal Bayesian Stopping for Efficient Inference of Consistent LLM Answers

evidence.note: Trains reasoning models to be concise in proportion to difficulty by modulating the token penalty and the target length per problem, and fixes a distortion that naive reward weighting introduces into group-normalized RL.
evidence.title: The Overthinker's DIET: Cutting Token Calories with DIfficulty-AwarE Training

evidence.note: Proves that parameterizing an outcome reward as the log-likelihood ratio between a policy and a reference model makes the per-step Q value fall out of the same model for free, so a process reward model can be obtained by training an outcome reward model on response-level labels alone.
evidence.title: Free Process Rewards without Process Labels

evidence.note: Gives two aggregation algorithms whose failure probability provably decays to zero as inference compute grows, assuming only that the model can sometimes be right and can compare two solutions better than chance.
evidence.title: Provable Scaling Laws for the Test-Time Compute of Large Language Models

evidence.note: Introduces EDIS, a trajectory-level score that measures how unstably token entropy evolves during generation, and uses it to select better reasoning rollouts at inference and to curate training samples in RL.
evidence.title: EDIS: Diagnosing LLM Reasoning via Entropy Dynamics

name: majority voting
